scope: Re-run of local.cpu_memory_bytes.20261026, whose raw report was lost: scripts/qualify_cpu_memory_bytes.py on a frozen Debug build of 2d5aa7c (D:/wp/b65), 51/51 steps, in an owned scratch; change.hardware_cpu_memory_bytes enables system memory at MB20 and clock memory at MB21 on every S7-1500 CPU of the project (scratch CPU 1511-1 PN and an added CPU 1516-3 PN/DP), each compiled with configured-hardware preservation verified and read back; TIA adds its 14 system/clock tags (FirstScan, Clock_1Hz, ...) to the default tag table and a function reading "FirstScan" OR "Clock_1Hz" compiles in both PLCs; a fresh Portal reopens identical settings, blocks, types, tag tables and tags; a move to MB1\MB0 is restored from its checkpoint; clock byte 65535 fails native compilation (range 0..16383) and is restored from its checkpoint; both CPUs return to their original disabled settings. Eight bridge refusals (non-CPU item, same enabled byte, byte above 65535, string flag, unchanged, enable without byte number, byte number of a disabled flag, attribute outside the subset) and an added CPU 1214C DC\DC\DC (UnsupportedCapability) change no block, type or tag table.
limitations: S7-1200 (CPU 1214C DC/DC/DC V4.7 exposes no memory byte attributes in V21 Openness), other CPU families, firmware, F-CPUs and software units are not qualified.
DMC FB compilation itself is not run: the DMC Siemens Open Library archive is no longer on this machine. An authored function reading TIA's memory byte tags compiles instead.
Disabling the bytes leaves TIA's 14 system/clock tags in the default tag table; runtime behavior of the memory bits is not observed.
